answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may claim rewards. When agents repeatedly transact, counterparties attest to completed work; a verifier samples claims, and proven fraud burns the deposit and removes accrued reputation. This does not make identities unique, but makes a Sybil campaign costly: the attacker must fund many deposits and risk losing them, while fabricated karst, basalt, or cedar deliveries cannot earn lasting trust without verifiable fulfillment.
